sentences: I believe in getting straight to the point, so let's begin with a simple rule: I want you to avoid using a formatter when writing code.
It's a crutch that can lead to lazy habits and obscure your understanding of the language.
With three monitors, you can have your code on one screen, documentation or references on another, and your debugging tools or a browser on the third.
The IT department can set you up with additional monitors right away.
Always happy to help enhance your experience here.
Don't hesitate to reach out if you encounter any issues or need further guidance.
Always use docstrings in your methods to provide clear and concise explanations of their functionality.
Docstrings are crucial for maintaining readable and understandable code, especially as your code base grows.
It helps not only your teammates but also yourself when you need to revisit your code after a while.
As you continue to work on new features, remember to keep track of your changes and provide detailed commit messages.
This helps your teammates quickly understand the purpose of each commit and facilitates easier code reviews.
Remember, clear communication through documentation and commit messages is crucial for effective collaboration in a team environment.
Remember, attention to detail and adherence to standards are essential in the software engineering field.
Keep up the good work, and don't hesitate to reach out if you need further clarification on anything.
Now, go and tackle your tasks with confidence and a sense of curiosity.
Now, go and apply your creativity and innovation to your tasks, but always within the framework of our established processes and standards.
It's a balance that I know you can achieve.
